analysis: All three changed files are test-only (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/...), so no production code paths, trust boundaries, keys or authorization logic change. Examined: (1) UnreclaimableLoadMemoryFixture.swift adds a lock-protected ScriptedCounter and a superLoads counter inside the scripted Super loader (lines 6-12, 67, 117-124). The loader still always throws, so no weights load and no real model memory is touched. The fixture uses temporary directories and a ws://127.0.0.1:0 coordinator URL, so no network exposure. (2) ProviderLifecycleTests.swift adds a test that a drain with the coordinator connection down finishes (lines 210-230) and a test that shutdown completes when a slot is stuck unloading (lines 232-254). These document intended lifecycle behavior (TB-002 and the availability aspects of T-010). They use unreachable ws://unused.invalid and an in-memory fake client. (3) ProviderModelSwitchTests.swift adds a test asserting the daemon state's enabled_models_at_last_switch is reported only after an accepted commit and that the saved config matches (lines 189-229). It uses MockCoordinator and temp files. No secrets, real credentials, or persistent artifacts are introduced; temp roots are removed via defer. Residual question for integration: the production behaviors these tests assert (drain acknowledgment with the connection down, shutdown bound for an unproven native retirement, daemon-state reporting of the applied filter) live in non-supplied source files, so I could not verify their implementation or whether they weaken the drain-acknowledgment or revocation semantics in T-053/TB-011. Nothing in the supplied evidence indicates a regression.
